summary: Hancock County, ME steel lookout tower ordered 1921 and erected 1922 on Dedham Bald; dismantled in 2009 and moved to Canada; summit now has communication towers.

facts.design: steel lookout tower: 47 feet in the 1921 order, 60 feet in the AMC article (sources disagree)
facts.status_note: Dismantled in 2009 and moved to Canada per Forest Lookouts and AMC Maine; concrete stanchions remain at the spot; the summit has communication towers

access.note: Two hiking guides describe a walk to the summit from a roadside trailhead; neither says who owns the land

visit.trail_note: About 0.6 to 0.7 miles from Bald Mountain Road; the trail is not signed or blazed and is steep on bedrock near the top

events.note: Permanent camp built on Bald Mountain before the tower

Forest Commissioner Samuel T. Dana announced on October 27, 1921 that the state had ordered material for a 47-foot steel lookout tower; Dedham, Otis and Mariaville requested it and were to bear about 40 per cent of the cost
Erection reported under way in April 1922; the AMC article says it was erected in 1921
A. F. Moore, a surveyor, announced to act as lookout at the station
Fred Barnes employed as summer lookout, per a November 1922 Ellsworth American item
360-degree panoramic map centered on the tower made in 1923
Dedham-Bald lookout part of a 1930 fire district of sixteen towns with a district fire warden; the Forest Commissioner's annual report called it highly successful
Dismantled and moved to Canada; Forest Lookouts says removed in November 2009 with plans to relocate it the following year

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The October 1921 order says a 47-foot steel tower; the AMC article says the 1921 tower was 60 feet. Both are recorded in the story and height_m is left unset.
AMC says the tower was erected in 1921; the Forest Lookouts quotes from the Ellsworth American show erection still under way in April 1922. Both years are recorded.

Maine by Foot (posted 2019) describes walking to 'the old fire tower at the top' and lists remnants of the past. The AMC article and Forest Lookouts say the tower was dismantled in 2009 and only concrete stanchions remain. The tower is treated as gone; the trail guide wording is treated as loose.
AMC gives 1,261 feet; Maine by Foot gives 1,237 feet. Not used in facts.

sources.title: A Fine Hike on Dedham Bald Mountain, One of 15 "Bald" Mountains in Maine

notes_for_editor: Fate is well supported (two sources agree on 2009 removal to Canada). Open conflicts: 47 ft (1921 order) vs 60 ft (AMC); 1921 vs April 1922 erection; 1,261 ft vs 1,237 ft summit. Maine by Foot's 'old fire tower at the top' wording is loose against AMC and Forest Lookouts. Access level 'public' is inferred from two hiking guides; land ownership was not found. Do not confuse with the Bald Mountain (Washington County, US 85) tower in the Maine History Online slideshow.
